ebr-p4.s: (The fourteenth goddess is) Gná. Frigg sends her into various worlds on her errands. She has the horse that runs through sky and sea and is called Hófvarpnir. It happened once, as she was riding, that some of the Vanir saw her ride through the air. Then one of them said:

ebr-p8.s: And when Þórr came to Geirröðr's, he and his companion were first shown to a goat-shed for lodging, and there was one chair to sit on, and Þórr sat on it. Then he became aware that the chair was rising under him up towards the roof. He thrust the staff Gríðarvölr up into the rafters and let himself press down hard on the chair. Then there was a great crack, followed by a scream. Geirröðr's daughters, Gjálp and Greip, had been under the chair, and he had broken the backs of both. Then Þórr said:

ebr-p13.s: 1. These fragments are gathered from the manuscripts of Snorra Edda, except the last, which is from Völsunga saga. They are either remnants of lost Eddic poems or stanzas in the Eddic manner that have stood on their own from the beginning. Their matter comes both from the myths of the gods and from heroic legends. (Guðni Jónsson, Eddulyklar 1949)
